title: Cremona and the Second Battle of Bedriacum
lead: A Roman colony on the Padus in northern Italy. The Flavianist and Vitellianist armies fought a night battle near it in October AD 69, and the Flavianists then stormed the camp and sacked the city for four days.

sections.b: Wikipedia dates the second battle of Bedriacum to 24 October 69. Tacitus says Cremona was founded 286 years earlier, in the time of Hannibal (3:34), and that after the sack only the temple of Mefitis outside the walls remained standing (3:33). Antonius afterward forbade keeping Cremonans as captives, and the town was rebuilt. Josephus tells the fall of Cremona more briefly (War 4.11.2-3, Whiston's numbering): he has Antonius allow his soldiers to plunder it and counts 30,200 dead of Vitellius's army against 4,500 of Antonius's men. Those are Josephus's figures, not checked against anything else; Tacitus has 40,000 armed men burst into the town (3:33).
